raw_text:
Summary and approach
- Client: 28 F, recreational lifter, regular 28-day cycle. Severe primary dysmenorrhea — flow days 1–3 (debilitating pelvic pressure and cramping) require absolutely no high-intensity work, no heavy Valsalva lifting, no jumping. GP cleared exercise otherwise.
- Programme length: 12 weeks, start date 2026-06-01.
- Goal: steady strength progression while respecting cycle restrictions by phasing intensity around the menstrual cycle so the client can train consistently each month and make progress.
- Structure: 4-week microcycles mapped to the client’s cycle. Each 28-day block will align roughly to:
  - Menstrual window (cycle days 1–3): low-intensity, low-load, no high effort or high intra‑abdominal pressure movements, emphasis on mobility, light aerobic, pain-management-friendly strength (bodyweight / light load), diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor awareness.
  - Follicular build (cycle days 4–13): moderate volume, increasing intensity; good time for technique and strength work.
  - Ovulatory/late follicular to early luteal (cycle days 14–21): peak strength and highest-intensity lifting (heavy-ish, but avoid Valsalva only on flow days — otherwise cleared). This is the primary heavy-strength window.
  - Luteal (cycle days 22–28, excluding overlap with next menses): moderate intensity, slightly reduced volume as needed, more tempo-based reps and conditioning that’s not high-impact; taper into menstrual window.
- Because the client’s last period started 2026-05-01 and cycles are 28 days, her next periods would begin:
  - 2026-05-29 (but we start programme on 2026-06-01 — she will be cycle day ~4 on 2026-06-01).
  - For planning, I will assume standard 28-day cycles each month; indicate how to adapt if exact dates shift.
- Weekly training frequency: 3 strength sessions per week + 1–2 optional low-impact aerobic / mobility sessions. Strength sessions are full-body with emphasis on progressive overload during higher-intensity cycle windows. During menstrual days 1–3 sessions are replaced with low-load alternatives.
- Progression model: 3-week intensity/volume progression with a lighter week or an auto-regulated week as needed; over 12 weeks this yields steady increases in load/reps where allowed by cycle phase.

How to use the plan
- Track cycle day each day. On cycle days 1–3, follow the “flow-day” session listed instead of the usual weekly session(s).
- If severe symptoms occur outside days 1–3, treat them as a flow day and use the low-intensity options.
- If on a high-intensity day but feeling winded or unable to Valsalva safely, reduce load by 20–40% and use more breath-focused technique (exhale on exertion, bracing without forceful breath-hold).
- Warm-ups: 8–12 minutes general warm-up (light cardio, dynamic mobility). Add specific warm-up sets for each main lift, especially in heavy phases.
- Cool-down: 5–10 minutes of mobility and diaphragmatic breathing, heat or TENS as advised by GP if helpful for cramps.
- Nutrition and recovery: guidelines below; adjust to client preferences and energy needs.

12-week plan (start 2026-06-01)
Notes on dates and cycle mapping for first month:
- Her previous period started 2026-05-01. With 28-day cycles she would be:
  - 2026-05-29: cycle day 1 (start of next menses),
  - 2026-06-01: cycle day 4 (i.e., she will be just coming out of flow days and entering follicular build). So week 1 begins in follicular build. I’ll provide each week’s plan and highlight when to swap in flow-day sessions the next time her cycle days 1–3 occur (e.g., next menses around 2026-06-26–06-28 depending on exact start). The weekly structure is cycle-aware, but you must always check cycle day before each session and replace with the menstrual (flow) session on cycle days 1–3.

Macro layout
- Weeks 1–4: Establish baseline, build technique and moderate volume; week 4 is deload/auto-regulate.
- Weeks 5–8: Increase load and intensity; week 8 is lighter week.
- Weeks 9–12: Peak strength blocks with slightly higher intensity in ovulatory window, then taper at end of each 4-week cycle.

Weekly structure (applies each week; sessions A/B/C alternate across the week):
- Session A (Lower emphasis): compound hip-dominant + accessory
- Session B (Upper emphasis): horizontal push/pull + accessory
- Session C (Full-body / squat emphasis): squat pattern + posterior chain
- Optional: Low-impact aerobic / mobility session mid-week or on active recovery day.

Strength sessions: typically 45–60 minutes.

Progression cues
- Follicular & ovulatory windows (cycle days ~4–21): push progression — increase load 2.5–5% when prescribed reps are achieved for two consecutive sessions.
- Luteal (cycle days ~22–28): maintain load if fatigued; focus on technique and slightly slower tempo (3–1–1 ecc/iso/concentric when needed).
- Menstrual (cycle days 1–3): perform the prescribed low-load, low-intensity session only.

Detailed 12-week program
Week 1 (2026-06-01 to 06-07) — Baseline, entering follicular build (cycle day ~4)
Goal: reinforce technique, moderate volume
Sessions (3x/week; pick non-consecutive days, e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri)

Session A — Lower / Hip-dominant
- Warm-up: 8 min brisk walk + dynamic hip swings, glute activation
- Romanian deadlift (RDL) — 3 sets x 6–8 reps @ RPE 6–7 (moderate)
- Split squat (rear foot elevated) — 3 x 8 each leg (bodyweight or light DB)
- Glute bridge or hip thrust — 3 x 10
- Pallof press — 3 x 10 each side (anti-rotation)
- Farmer carry — 3 x 45–60s walk at moderate load
- Cool-down: pelvic tilts, diaphragmatic breathing 5 min

Session B — Upper / Horizontal
- Warm-up: band pull-aparts, shoulder circles
- Bench press (or DB floor press) — 3 x 6–8 @ RPE 6–7
- Bent-over row or single-arm DB row — 3 x 8–10
- Overhead band or light DB press — 3 x 10
- Face pulls — 3 x 12–15
- Plank — 3 x 30–45s (diaphragmatic breathing)
- Cool-down: pec/shoulder stretch

Session C — Full-body / Squat
- Warm-up: ankle/hip mobility, bodyweight squats
- Goblet squat (or barbell back squat if comfortable) — 3 x 6–8
- Deadlift (conventional or trap bar) light to moderate — 3 x 5
- Step-ups — 3 x 8 each leg
- Romanian chair/side-lying clams — 3 x 12 each side
- Farmers carry or suitcase carry — 3 x 45s
- Cool-down: foam rolling, pelvic floor breathing

Optional: 1–2 low-impact cardio/mobility sessions (20–30 min cycling, swimming, brisk walking). Avoid high impact and jumping throughout programme only on flow days 1–3; otherwise small jumps allowed when cleared during ovulation windows, but we will avoid jumping altogether per client restrictions on flow days only — outside flow she’s cleared for normal lifts.

Week 2 (06-08 to 06-14) — Follicular build
Goal: Slight increase in volume/intensity
- Session A: RDL 4 x 6, Split squat 3 x 8–10, Hip thrust 3 x 8–10, Pallof 3 x 12, Suitcase carry 3 x 60s
- Session B: Bench 4 x 6, Bent-over row 4 x 8, OHP 3 x 8, Face pull 3 x 15, Dead bug 3 x 10 each
- Session C: Back squat 4 x 6 (moderate), Deadlift 3 x 4 (moderate), Bulgarian split 3 x 8, Glute med work 3 x12
- Progress: increase load by 2.5–5% if top-end reps achieved comfortably.

Week 3 (06-15 to 06-21) — Follicular → Ovulatory; peak of strength window approaching
Goal: Push intensity on main lifts
- Session A: RDL 4 x 5 (slightly heavier), Front-loaded split squats 3 x 6–8, Hip thrust 4 x 6–8, Anti-rotation 3 x10
- Session B: Bench 5 x 5 (work to heavier load), Barbell row 4 x 6, OHP 3 x 6, High-rep face pull 3 x15
- Session C: Back squat 5 x 5, Deadlift 4 x 4 (build to challenging but not maximal), Step-ups 3 x 6–8
- Note: Watch breathing technique for heavy lifts (avoid prolonged Valsalva on flow days only; otherwise normal bracing ok).

Week 4 (06-22 to 06-28) — Deload/Auto-regulate (this week includes expected next menses days 06-26 to 06-28 — cycle days 1–3 — so apply flow-day sessions when they fall)
Goal: recovery and consolidation
- If on flow days 1–3: perform Flow-Day protocol (below). If not on flow days: perform light sessions at ~60% volume and intensity of previous week.
Flow-day session (to replace any scheduled strength session on cycle days 1–3)
- Warm-up: 10 min gentle walk, pelvic rocking, diaphragmatic breathing, heat pack as needed
- Mobility & low-load strength circuit (x2–3 rounds, slow and controlled):
  - Glute bridge — 10–12 (bodyweight)
  - Bird dog — 8 each side slow
  - Side-lying clams — 12 each side
  - Seated band row (light) — 12
  - Seated leg extension or short-range step-ups — 10 each leg (bodyweight)
- Light core/mindful breathing: 5–8 min diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor relaxation exercises
- Gentle stretching, 10–15 min total. Emphasize pain management and rest.
- No heavy lifts, no jumping, no high intensity.

Weeks 5–8 (06-29 to 07-26) — Strength block 2
General: Increase intensity across weeks 5–7 with week 8 as a lighter week. Continue to replace any session that falls on cycle days 1–3 with the flow-day protocol.

Week 5 (strength emphasis)
- Session A: RDL 4 x 5–6 (heavier), Bulgarian split squat 4 x 6–8, Hip thrust 3 x 6–8, Farmer carry 4 x 60s
- Session B: Incline DB press or bench 4 x 5–6, Pendlay/Barbell row 4 x 6, OHP 4 x 6, Face pulls 4 x 12
- Session C: Back squat 4 x 5, Deadlift 4 x 3–5 (heavy-ish), Accessory glute/hamstring 3 x 10

Week 6 (intensity maintained)
- Slightly more volume on accessory lifts; main lifts 3–5 sets in target rep ranges (5–6). Increase loads where appropriate.

Week 7 (peak intensity in ovulatory window)
- Main lifts enter heavy 3–5 reps ranges where applicable:
  - Session A: RDL 5 x 4–5, Split squat 4 x 6, Hip thrust 4 x 5
  - Session B: Bench 5 x 3–5 (work to a heavy 3–5RM), Row 4 x 5, OHP 4 x 5
  - Session C: Back squat 5 x 3–5, Deadlift heavy singles or triples 4 x 1–3 (only if not on menstrual days)
- Note: If a heavy day falls on flow days 1–3, replace with flow session. If heavy day falls in luteal and client feels unwell, reduce load and focus on speed/technique.

Week 8 (deload / lighter)
- Reduce volume and intensity by ~40%. Emphasize movement quality. Any flow days follow flow protocol.

Weeks 9–12 (07-27 to 08-23) — Final strength block & consolidation
Goal: final push for strength with conservative peaking; maintain cycle-aware modifications.

Week 9
- Reintroduce slightly higher volume targeting progressive overload from previous peak. Main lifts 4 x 4–6; accessories 3 x 8–12.

Week 10
- More intensity; main lifts 3–5 x 3–5; include some variations (paused squats, deficit deadlifts) for technical strength. If ovulatory window (high strength capacity), target heavier loads.

Week 11
- Peak week: test rep maxes or train heavy across main lifts with conservative approach — e.g., work sets up to 3RM or 5RM depending on comfort. Avoid maximal Valsalva efforts on predicted menstrual days.

Week 12
- Taper/deload: lower volume by 40–60%. Focus on recovery, technique, and consolidate gains. Use flow-day sessions for menstrual days.

Example month (how cycle-specific weeks might map across calendar)
- Because the client’s cycle is regular, each 28-day program block will align similarly: the first 3 days of each cycle are flow days — replace any scheduled session on those days with the Flow-day session. The strongest/most intense sessions should be scheduled for cycle days ~9–16 where possible.

Flow-day practical recommendations (critical)
- Absolutely no heavy Valsalva lifting; avoid maximal or near-maximal loads.
- No jumping or high-impact movement on days 1–3.
- Prioritize:
  - Diaphragmatic breathing and pelvic-floor-focused cues (e.g., breathe out on exertion, avoid bracing that feels like bearing down).
  - Heat, gentle massage, TENS (if client uses and GP agrees), OTC analgesics as recommended by GP.
  - Low-load strength, isometrics, gentle core work, and mobility.
- Intensity guideline: RPE ≤ 5 on flow days.
- If cramps are severe, encourage rest and gentle movement only.

Nutrition and recovery guidance
- Calorie/protein: aim for a moderate calorie intake to support strength gains. Protein ~1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight per day (adjust to bodyweight). Distribute protein across meals.
- Hydration: maintain hydration especially during luteal phase when fluid retention is possible. Warm fluids and magnesium (under GP guidance) may help cramps.
- Micronutrients: ensure adequate iron (menstrual losses), vitamin D, and magnesium as indicated by blood tests / GP advice. If heavy menstrual bleeding exists, check ferritin with GP.
- Pre- and post-workout: on flow days, keep meals light and easily digestible. On high-intensity days, ensure sufficient carbohydrate before workouts.
- Sleep and stress: prioritize 7–9 hours sleep and stress management (breathing, yoga, light walks) — stress can worsen dysmenorrhea.

Technical & safety coaching
- Teach diaphragmatic breathing and pelvic floor relaxation vs bearing down. Cue exhale on exertion and avoid forceful breath-holding during flow days.
- Use belt or heavy bracing only when comfortable and not on flow days if it increases pelvic pressure.
- Monitor symptoms and adjust: if severe pain occurs, reduce load further or rest and consult GP.

How to progress week to week
- When prescribed rep ranges are completed with good form and RPE lower than target for two sessions, increase load 2.5–5% on the next suitable session (avoid increasing load right before predicted flow days).
- For accessory work, progress reps or reduce rest between sets.
- Keep written training log and note cycle day and symptom severity to refine future scheduling.

If symptoms change
- If dysmenorrhea becomes more limiting, shift heavier work to mid-cycle and increase frequency of flow-day replacement sessions. If symptoms improve, you can be more aggressive with load increases.

Final notes
- This plan emphasizes cycle-aware periodization so the client can safely progress while managing dysmenorrhea. It’s adaptable: each day, check cycle day and symptom severity and swap to the Flow-day session if needed.
- If you want, I can convert this into a day-by-day calendar for the exact dates between 2026-06-01 and 2026-08-23, or tailor sets/loads to your client’s 1RMs and bodyweight. Which would you prefer?
